subject: reasoning
question: In a certain code language, 'MOBILE' is written as 'NQEMQK' and 'BISHOP' is written as 'CKVLTV'. How will 'CHARGE' be written in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

For, ‘MOBILE is written as NQEMQK.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b9d6ad559170fd3bfc2500394ee73b9be6d8f68b477b23b05b15f79f1669ba6b.png] 

 

 

 

For, 'BISHOP is written as 'CKVLTV',

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96f68785010567abb73aeb6af83f954381ae932c9e4a2d36de9975003d8db0ea.png] 

 

Similarly, for 'CHARGE'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ec79549fcc581038e2f7316eed31abe2c7e8bf11eb0ec3d840fa8d969e4d5ad.png] 

So, 'CHARGE' will be written as '**DJDVLK**'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
